source.title: The Depth Delusion: Why Transformers Should Be Wider, Not Deeper

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It contains internal inconsistencies in reported methods and results, noted under problems.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests architecture effects on language-model loss and argues that depth and width are not interchangeable, challenging the claim that architecture shape has little effect at a fixed parameter count. It also fits an architecture-conditioned loss model.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-loss results for 30 configurations and a fitted architecture-conditioned loss model. Its gradient-persistence measurements are also recorded, but they do not measure any listed claim version. Statements about GPT-3, PaLM and other prior models are audits or cited context, not new experimental results on those models.
record.test_reason: The study trains depth-width variants at near-matched parameter counts (about 1B, 3B and 7B) and argues against Kaplan's claim that loss depends on N, not shape. That bears directly on V4. Its compute-optimal exponents are derived analytically, not measured, and its loss-law fit leaves the capacity exponent unidentified.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that beyond a critical depth (∝W^0.44, about 2.43 log W) extra layers raise loss, and that width should grow faster than depth (derived D*∝C^0.12, W*∝C^0.34). They recommend never exceeding D≈2.5 log W, and say extrapolation to 100B+ models needs validation.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies transformer depth and width and fits an architecture-conditioned loss model, rather than reproducing the original scaling-law measurements or compute-optimal training recipe. It does not test small-run extrapolation or run a controlled compute-budget allocation sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Loss changes with depth and width in the reported architecture sweeps. The paper reports a power-law versus logarithmic fit comparison for gradient persistence, but not sensitivity of the loss-law fit to alternative fitting methods or training setups.

fits_no_version.finding: Fitted gradient persistence length grows as W^0.44 (R2 0.98), better than a log W fit (R2 0.60).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In tested transformers, per-layer gradient persistence grows sublinearly with width.

record.code_released: not stated; the text says code and training logs will be released upon acceptance but provides no URL
record.problems: The paper reports single-seed runs and says the standard errors are estimated over the final 10% of training tokens, not across independent seeds. The text is internally inconsistent about implementation details: the main setup says GELU and Pre-LN, while the appendix says SwiGLU and RMSNorm; the 7B deep model is reported with width 2816 and 6.38B parameters in the main results but width 2896 and 7.08B parameters in the extended material. The claimed compute-optimal exponents are derived rather than directly tested in a compute-budget sweep. Several reported loss results have no stated uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported architecture loss configurations from Tables 6 and 10 were left out. Repeated appearances of the same configurations in the text and tables were not duplicated as rows.

untested.parts: No separate N, T or compute sweeps. The only fit is the architecture ansatz, whose capacity exponent is unidentified.
No small-run fit used to predict larger held-out runs.
D*∝C^0.12 and W*∝C^0.34 are derived from the ansatz using Kaplan's exponents. There is no compute-budget sweep, and token allocation is not tested.
No comparison of loss-law exponents across fitting choices or setups.

missing.what: Learning-rate and batch-size sweep at D=16. Loss ranges from 3.01 to 3.15 across LR/BS, comparable to the shape effects reported. A single LR was used for all depths, a possible confound for V4.
missing.locator: Appendix A.1, Extended Hyperparameter Sweep table

missing.what: Large-scale configurations reported with different widths and parameter counts in Table 10 than in Table 6. Which runs were trained is unclear.
Per-run token counts for the 1B–7B runs are not stated. The FLOPs footnote implies about 140B tokens for both 7B runs. The appendix says Chinchilla-optimal tokens, conflicting with the main text.

record.verdict_notes: V4 evidence is mixed. Within moderate shapes, loss varies by about 1%, consistent with Kaplan. Very deep shapes lose 3–6%. All runs are single seed, with SEs taken from within-run token windows, so gaps under about 0.03 nats are not reliably distinguishable. Internal inconsistencies are serious: the 1B–7B widths and parameter counts differ between tables, the main text says GELU/Pre-LN while the appendix says SwiGLU/RMSNorm, and the Dcrit values in Figure 4 and the text disagree. The V3 derivation plugs in Kaplan's α=0.076 rather than the paper's own fitted α=0.22, and contains a dubious step (D/W=1/2 'in exponent space'). The model audits of GPT-3, PaLM and Llama are extrapolations, not results.

versions.untested_parts: It does not isolate parameter, token and compute power laws in separate sweeps, or establish the non-bottleneck regime across several orders of magnitude. Its fitted loss model includes an architecture penalty.
No small-run fit is used to predict the loss of separately held-out, much larger runs.
The claimed depth and width exponents are derived from an ansatz and exponents attributed to Kaplan et al.; the study does not run a controlled compute-budget sweep or test token-count growth.
The paper compares configurations with similar, not exactly identical, parameter counts; it does not systematically isolate every architecture detail.
Only autoregressive language modeling on web text is studied; other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested.

The study compares alternative fits for gradient persistence, but does not test how scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations change across parameter counting, schedules, data or fitting choices.

rows.subject: 30-architecture aggregate
rows.operation_detail: Fit the proposed architecture-conditioned loss ansatz to the 30 configurations using nonlinear least squares.
rows.note: The fitted model has separate capacity and data terms plus an architecture penalty; the text does not report a separate fitted token exponent here.
rows.check: The ansatz fit's capacity exponent CI [–0.21, 0.65] includes zero. The fit cannot show a power law in N, and N and T are confounded across the baseline (6.4B tokens) and large-scale (up to 140B) runs.

relation.reason: The study reports its own depth-width comparisons at approximately matched parameter scales, directly bearing on V4.

tranche.reason: The architecture sweeps and explicit argument seek to qualify or overturn shape invariance; the compute-optimal exponents are analytical claims rather than measured compute sweeps.

source_check.notes: Loss is per-token training cross-entropy used as a validation proxy; SEs measure final-window variation in single-seed runs. Architecture tables conflict, individual large-run token budgets are unstated, and the reported optimal-scaling exponents are derived rather than empirically measured.
